intro: Lesson 18: Asia's physical features: monsoons and droughts. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

panels.title: Mountains and plateaus
points: Tibetan Plateau: the 'roof of the world'
Formed by India pushing into Asia

panels.title: Rivers, seas and deserts
points: Dead Sea: lowest land on Earth

model.title: Why do monsoon floods hit Bangladesh hard?

parts.text: Most of the country is a low, flat delta
Huge rivers carry monsoon rain from the Himalayas
Rivers overflow onto the flat land
Many people live on the fertile flood plains

parts.label: Why it works
parts.text: Low, flat land plus huge river flows puts many people at risk

keywords.def: a large area of high, flat land
a seasonal wind that brings a wet season
a long period with too little rain
flat land at a river mouth built from sediment
the height and shape of the land

questions.q: Why does the land heat faster than the sea?
questions.a: Land heats and cools quickly; water stores heat

questions.q: What is the 'roof of the world'?
Give one benefit of the monsoon.
questions.a: Rain for crops such as rice, water supply

questions.q: Core: Label Asia's main physical features on the map, then explain the monsoon in the portal response box using a labelled sequence.
questions.a: Accurate map; a clear four-step monsoon explanation

questions.q: Extend: Explain how a weak monsoon causes drought and why that matters.
questions.a: Less rain, failed crops, water shortages, rising food prices

questions.q: Stretch: Why does the same monsoon bring floods in one place and drought in another?
questions.a: Rain varies by relief, distance from the sea and timing; some areas are in rain shadow

questions.q: The summer monsoon in South Asia brings:
questions.a: B) Moist winds and heavy rain. Low pressure over hot land draws in moist winds from the Indian Ocean.

questions.q: Big question: floods and drought in one year?
questions.a: Monsoon rain is concentrated in a few months; too much then, too little the rest of the year or if it fails
